title: The New Neighbour
summary: Sam does not like the noisy new family next door, until one rainy evening changes everything.
paragraphs: Sam had lived in the same small flat for eight years. He liked his quiet life. Every morning he drank his coffee by the window, read the news on his phone and watered the plants on his balcony. In the evening he cooked a simple dinner and went to bed early. Nothing ever changed, and that was exactly how he wanted it.

Then, in March, a new family moved into the flat next door. There was a mother, a father, two young boys and a very large dog. From the first day, the flat was full of noise. The boys ran up and down the stairs. The dog barked at every person who walked past. On Saturday mornings the father played loud music while he cleaned the kitchen.

Sam was not happy. Twice he knocked on their door to complain. The mother, a tall woman called Lina, always said sorry with a warm smile. “The boys are still getting used to the new place,” she explained. But the noise did not stop, and Sam started to avoid the family on the stairs.

One evening in April, there was a terrible storm. The wind was so strong that it broke a window in Sam's living room. Rain was coming in, and water was running across the floor towards his books. Sam tried to cover the window with a piece of plastic, but he could not hold it and fix it at the same time.

Suddenly there was a knock at the door. It was Lina's husband, Omar, with a box of tools. “We heard the glass break,” he said. “Can I help?” Behind him stood the two boys, holding towels. Without waiting for an answer, they started to dry the floor and move the books to a safe place.

Omar and Sam worked together for almost an hour. When the window was finally covered, Lina appeared with a pot of hot soup. They all sat on Sam's sofa, tired and wet, and ate dinner together while the storm continued outside. The dog lay at Sam's feet and fell asleep.

After that night, Sam's life was a little less quiet, but much happier. On Saturdays he sometimes joined Omar in the kitchen, and the boys taught him how to play their favourite video game. He still drank his coffee by the window every morning. But now, when he heard the dog barking, he just smiled.

questions.question: Why was Sam unhappy when the new family arrived?
options: They made a lot of noise
questions.explanation: The boys ran on the stairs, the dog barked and the father played loud music, so the flat was full of noise.

questions.question: What happened during the storm?
options: The lights in the building went out
A window in Sam's flat broke
questions.explanation: The text says the wind was so strong that it broke a window in Sam's living room.

questions.question: How did the boys help?
options: They dried the floor and moved the books
questions.explanation: The boys came with towels, dried the floor and moved the books to a safe place.

questions.question: How did Sam feel about the family at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: He joins Omar on Saturdays, plays games with the boys and smiles when the dog barks.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the story?
options: People can change our lives in good ways
Dogs should not live in flats
It is important to cook simple meals
questions.explanation: The family Sam disliked becomes an important and happy part of his life.

grammar.explanation: We use the past perfect for something that happened before another moment in the past. Here, the eight years happened before the family arrived.
grammar.example: Sam had lived in the same small flat for eight years.

exercise.question: Which sentence uses the past perfect correctly?
options: When Omar arrived, the window has already broken.
When Omar arrived, the window had already broken.
When Omar arrived, the window already breaks.
When Omar arrived, the window was already break.
exercise.explanation: The window broke before Omar arrived, so we use had + past participle: had broken.

grammar.explanation: We use was/were + -ing to describe an action that was in progress when something else happened.
grammar.example: Rain was coming in, and water was running across the floor towards his books.

exercise.question: Choose the correct form: They ___ dinner when the storm started.
exercise.explanation: The eating was in progress when the storm started, so we use the past continuous: were eating.
